audits.title: 2833 Quality improvement project on increasing antimicrobial stewardship and patient safety
audits.standard: Microguide local antimicrobial guidance; indication, route, duration and choice of antibiotic
audits.setting: Six geriatric wards, Broomfield Hospital, Mid-South Essex NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 99 of 168 patients on antibiotics; Microguide compliance 39-65% (mean 53%); indication and duration on drug charts 89%.

audits.intervention: Weekly microbiology consultant-led ward rounds, education for junior doctors, nurses and consultants, streamlined IT access to Microguide, AMS meetings and prescribing in simulation sessions.

cycle2.result: Compliance 70-90% (mean 83%); indication and duration on drug charts 95%.

audits.other_findings: Co-amoxiclav (n = 45) and Tazocin (n = 14) were the most used antibiotics; co-amoxiclav for UTI and Tazocin without microbiology approval were targeted.
audits.citation: Tarkas T, Suthahar Y. 2833 Quality improvement project on increasing antimicrobial stewardship and patient safety. Age and Ageing. 2025;54(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/ageing/afae277.018.

audits.title: 71 Electronic Prescribing Promotes Antimicrobial Stewardship In Surgery: A Closed-Loop Audit
audits.standard: Public Health England antimicrobial standards: documentation of allergy status, prescriber contact, indication and review/stop dates; appropriate antimicrobial choice and IV/total duration
audits.setting: West Middlesex University Hospital, surgical inpatients

cycle1.result: Prescriber contact details 69%, review/stop dates 17%, indications 78%, appropriate selection 76%, appropriate IV duration 63%, total duration 87%.

audits.intervention: Educational session, once-weekly microbiology round of surgical inpatients and introduction of electronic prescribing (Cerner).

cycle2.result: Prescriber contact details 100%, review/stop dates 100%, indications 96%, selection 90%, IV duration 93%, total duration 100%; p < 0.05 throughout.
